Subject: Re: significant latency in inference calls - production impact

Hey Marcus,

We saw a sharp spike in 99th percentile latency between 08:38-09:06 PDT this morning for our us-west deployment. Several customer-facing flows timed out and fell back to cached responses — we estimate approximately 18% error/slo failures across the peak window.

This affected our checkout service for a subset of customers and caused revenue impact. Can you confirm whether this is a platform-side regression and what remediation/redress is available? We need:
- an incident timeline and root cause
- proposed credits or goodwill gesture to offset the business impact
- an extension to our trial (we're in a promotional uplift period) so our evaluation isn't penalized

Appreciate a quick acknowledgement. We've opened a pager channel (pager@clearpath.health) and attached a brief syslog snippet for context.

Thanks,

Subject: RE: significant latency in inference calls - production impact

On Thu, Apr 15, 2027 at 9:22 AM PDT, Samantha Nguyen <samantha.nguyen@clearpath.health> wrote:
> We saw a sharp spike in 99th percentile latency between 08:38-09:06 PDT this morning...

We've confirmed an internal rollout triggered a less aggressive KV-cache warming policy for certain model variants in us-west. The immediate cause was a misapplied optimization that reduced prefix-cache population under heavy tail loads; this surfaced as elevated p99 latency for sequences > 512 tokens.

Actions taken:
- reverted the optimization at 09:12 PDT (service returned to baseline by 09:20 PDT)
- replayed requests against steady-state cluster to estimate impact
- collected artifacts and generated an incident note (attached)

Preliminary impact estimate: ~18% of requests in the window experienced latency above your SLA threshold; our telemetry suggests ~350k tokens affected across your org during the window.

Attaching: clearpath_postmortem.pdf (internal, contains timeline and artifacts) and logs bundle previously sent.

Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachments: clearpath_postmortem.pdf (4 pages)
JIRA: SUP-4567 (root-cause investigation ticket)

Thanks Hannah and Marcus — appreciate the fast turnaround and the postmortem. A couple of clarifying items from our side:
- The affected traffic was primarily production customers on our Enterprise tier. We estimate direct lost transactions ~ $9k during the 28-minute impact window plus downstream churn risk.
- Given this is an evaluation uplift, we're asking Redwood to consider an ex gratia credit to make us whole and a 30-day extension of our current trial uplift so procurement can complete without the incident penalizing evaluation metrics.

Is there an internal process for approving ex gratia credits? If you can put together a recommended credit amount and an approval path, we'll expedite sign-off on our end.
